## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 61 documents was traced to a source atom above. Items examined specifically:
- Derivational glosses with a source basis (not additions): "A batch with a single mileage posting has no duplicate. A mileage posting that already carries a reversal is not reversed again" (from dr_postings ≥ 2 and reverse_once); "A batch whose earnings entries already carry a long-distance pay component has had its bonus posted" (once per batch); "No submitted shown-pay shortfall dispute on the batch → Nothing" (baseline + `result … if sa_claims >= 1 else 0`); "It is read from the system's record of booked pay adjustments before the new one is approved" (evidence timing pre_action); "what the shopper says about other batches does not replace those records" (authority system_record).
- Tool-descriptive sentence "The tool computes no pay figure and checks no eligibility" (long_distance_bonus_posting): true of `task_tools.py` (atomic, no checks); descriptive, adds no obligation.
- No added confirmation, review, notification, step or ordering found. No "if unmet, first call …" guidance. No task world state written as policy fact (all worked figures are marked hypothetical; numeric coincidences checked — none mirrors this task's rows).
- Omissions / rewrites: none found.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of the four extended policies (rule, baseline, all 18 factor ladders with every tier, assembly order, overwrites) and of the governing base policies is carried at equal strength; the retired clauses are carried as retired and nothing else is retired; the three prerequisite sentences of this task stand verbatim, state form, in the blocked hubs only.

Policy-side note (not a KB verdict): `batch_ext_long_distance_bonus.baseline.rule` repeats, as the standard method, the same content as the base clause the policy's own `overwrite` retires ("long_distance is long_distance_bonus_usd when …"). The KB renders both faithfully — component_pay_rules §4 marks the former clause "under which the long-distance component was *simply* the batch type's long-distance bonus" as no longer in force, while long_distance_bonus_amount states the flat method as the computation document. A reader reconciles them (the flat method stands, the factors modify it), and the blind answer did, but the surface tension originates in the source.

## dependency_form

Scanned the whole product corpus using the blind hop marks (all hops state-derived, none pre-solved).
- Prerequisite sentences: each verbatim, state form, only in its blocked hub; same-form "Put the other way round / Read the other way" restatements in the same hub — never RED.
- Tool names: each hub names only its own tool (long_distance_bonus_posting → post_pay_component; duplicate_mileage_recovery → reverse_duplicate_pay; shown_pay_dispute_filing → submit_pay_dispute; shown_pay_adjustment_booking → book_pay_adjustment; likewise for task 1's three hubs). No factor, computation or base document names any tool.
- No state-form sentence restated as an action or with its performer; no route, checklist, dependency table or ordered cross-problem procedure; no depended-on document mentions who waits on it.
- Titles/openings: general subjects (the on_request hubs are titled by their request type — "Shown-Pay Shortfall Disputes …", which is that policy's general subject, not a mirror).
- Computation documents: none hints at a modifier ("unless otherwise", "adjustments may apply", exception lists — absent).
- Reviewed and not RED: (i) factor documents position themselves with generic conditionals — "after the claimed amount has been multiplied by any share applying to it", "once any goodwill applied to it has been subtracted", "the sum formed from the claimed amount (after any share applying to it) and any credits added to it". They carry the source's order of application without naming, overriding or pointing at a specific factor or document. (ii) long_distance_route_extension's "Two different thresholds" section and "the long-distance threshold that applies" come from the source ladder ("beyond the threshold that applies"); no document is named. (iii) long_distance_order_supplement's "not the orders listed on the offer" and similar boundary glosses clarify the rule's own input and do not describe a cross-problem mistake or name a tier a customer is on. (iv) The computation documents' "no submitted dispute → nothing" rows restate the baseline's own semantics inside the blocked policy's documents, in state form.

**Verdict: PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT RED).
